summary.text: Pete Ricketts is the Republican incumbent U.S. Senator from Nebraska. He worked for the family business that became Ameritrade, served as Governor of Nebraska from 2015 to 2023, and was appointed to the Senate in January 2023. He won the 2024 special election for the seat and is seeking election again; according to Ballotpedia's summary of his campaign website, he campaigns on tax cuts, border security and government efficiency.

paragraphs.text: Ricketts was born in Nebraska City and raised in Omaha, the son of an entrepreneur and a school teacher. He graduated from Westside High School and then earned a bachelor's degree in biology and an MBA in marketing and finance from the University of Chicago.

After graduate school he returned to Omaha and worked for Union Pacific before joining his family's business, which eventually became Ameritrade, as a customer services representative. His roles there included senior vice president of strategy and business development, senior vice president of marketing, president and chief operating officer.

Ricketts founded Drakon LLC, which supports Nebraska entrepreneurs and startup companies, and was a past board member of TD Ameritrade and the Chicago Cubs. He and three siblings purchased the Cubs and Wrigley Field in 2009.

He was sworn in as Nebraska's 40th Governor on January 8, 2015, succeeding Dave Heineman, and was re-elected in November 2018; Jim Pillen succeeded him in 2023. His Senate biography says he worked with the Legislature to deliver more than $12.7 billion in tax relief and cut the growth of state spending by more than half.

Gov. Jim Pillen appointed Ricketts to the U.S. Senate on January 12, 2023, to fill the vacancy created by Ben Sasse's resignation, and he was sworn in on January 23, 2023. In the November 2024 special general election he defeated Preston Love Jr. (D), 62.6% to 37.4%.
Ricketts serves on the Senate Environment and Public Works, Foreign Relations, Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs, and Budget committees.

According to his Senate biography, he serves on the board of the Mid-America Council of the Boy Scouts and as a director of the Nebraska Game and Parks Foundation. He lives in Omaha with his wife, Susanne Shore, and they have three children.
